items.text: You willnotbe tested on thismore detailed description ofhow soundsfrom a loudspeaker are heard.As the speaker cone moves to the right,it pushes air molecules closer together,creating a compression.These particles then push theright.Behind the compression as the speaker cone moves to the left is a region where the particles are spread out.This region is called a rarefaction.After the cone hasvibrated several times,it has created a series of compressions and rarefactions travelling away from it.Thisis a longitudinal sound wave(see page 98).When the waves enter the ear,they strike the eardrum and make it vibrate.These vibrations are changed into electrical signals,which are then detected by the brain
